issue_context.title: Inconsistent logger call in frameworksError wrapper
comments: If this is accepted as a valid issue, which is worth a fix, I can work on a pull request.

I think fastify's request/reply objects are not created when `frameworkErrors` happens.

Related to https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/4716

Worth investigating if we can create empty objects

They _are_ created, [here for bad url case](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/f4a8f3624c87ab23bec79280b876ad955ac5fafa/fastify.js#L697) and [here for async constraint error](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/f4a8f3624c87ab23bec79280b876ad955ac5fafa/fastify.js#L719).

It's just that logger is called before that. My suggestion is to call the logger after Fastify req/reply objects are created and only if `disableRequestLogging ` option is not set. In the same way [route does it](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/f4a8f3624c87ab23bec79280b876ad955ac5fafa/lib/route.js#L472).

uuuu you are right - I would go for it then!

I would not consider it breaking tho - if someone implemented the log serializer it should support both `req` formats. with your changes only one is required

review_comments: I might be missing something, but what if this is set to `true` or `undefined`/`null` instead, it would ever be called?

This is how it is checked in the other case when "incoming request" is logged, [in `route.js`](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/109873cf7e63eeffae65de2613d50b21815d3cb3/lib/route.js#L471)

I suppose `if (disableRequestLogging === false) {...}` was used because `false` is the default value for this option.

However, IMHO the more generic `if (!disableRequestLogging) {...}` would be better. For example like in `reply.js` [here](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/109873cf7e63eeffae65de2613d50b21815d3cb3/lib/reply.js#L606) and [here](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/109873cf7e63eeffae65de2613d50b21815d3cb3/lib/reply.js#L779).

>However, IMHO the more generic if (!disableRequestLogging) {...} would be better. For example like in reply.js [here](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/109873cf7e63eeffae65de2613d50b21815d3cb3/lib/reply.js#L606) and [here](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/109873cf7e63eeffae65de2613d50b21815d3cb3/lib/reply.js#L779).

Sure thing, that SGTM!

I just mixed things a little and got confused between the name of the variable and the value itself. Bad first impression 😅

To summarize, any value, which is not exactly `false`, will disable this default logging. I'd suggest to keep this implementation, otherwise it may break someone's code (for example, if empty string is used as a value).
